chunks: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him): 'Was God, Mighty and Majestic, aware of Himself before He created the creation?' He said: 'Yes.'

I said: 'Did He see it (His Self) and hear it?' He said: 'He was not in need of that, because He did not happen to ask it nor seek from it. He is His Self, and His Self is He. His Power is pervading. Thus, He is not in need of naming Himself.'

But He chose names for others to call Him by, because when He is not called by His Name, He would not be recognized. Thus, the first of what He chose for Himself was al-Ali al-Azim (the Exalted, the Magnificent), because He is loftier than all things. So its meaning is Allah, and His Name is al-Ali al-Azim — it is the first of His Names. He is Exalted above every thing.

key_terms.الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ: Al-Ali al-Azim — the Exalted, the Magnificent: the first divine Name, expressing absolute transcendence
key_terms.عَارِفاً بِنَفْسِهِ: Self-knowledge of God — divine self-awareness that is not dependent on sensory faculties
key_terms.قُدْرَتُهُ نَافِذَةٌ: His Power is pervading — divine omnipotence that encompasses all things without external instruments
key_terms.هُوَ نَفْسُهُ وَنَفْسُهُ هُوَ: He is His Self and His Self is He — absolute divine simplicity and self-identity

ai.seo_question: Did God know Himself before creating the world according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: In this profound theological dialogue, Ibn Sinan asks Imam al-Ridha (a.s.) whether God possessed self-knowledge before creation, and the Imam confirms this while explaining that God's knowing Himself transcends the creaturely modalities of seeing and hearing. The Imam articulates a sophisticated doctrine: God did not need sensory faculties to know Himself because He is absolutely identical with His Self and His Power is all-pervading. The divine Names were chosen not for God's own benefit but as a concession to creation, enabling creatures to recognize and call upon the Divine — the first such Name being al-Ali al-Azim (the Exalted, the Magnificent), reflecting God's absolute transcendence above all created things.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Al Husayn Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, and Musa Bin Umar, and Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Usman, from Ibn Sinan who said, 
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Was it that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Aware of Himself<sup>azwj</sup> before He<sup>azwj</sup> Created the creation?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.

I said, ‘He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Saw it (His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Self) and Heard (Himself<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>)?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> was not needy to that, because He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> did not happen to ask it nor seek from it. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Self, and His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Self is He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Power Implemented. Thus, He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is not needy that He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Hears Himself<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, but He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Chose Names for others to call Him<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> with these, because He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, when not called by His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Name, would not be recognised (by the creators).

Thus, the first of what He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Chose for Himself<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> was the Exalted, the Magnificent (الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ) because He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Loftier (than) the things, all of them. So its Meaning is Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Name is the Exalted, the Magnificent (الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ). It is the first of His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Names, Loftier upon every thing’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from al-Husayn ibn ‘Abdallah from Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah and Musa ibn ‘Umar and al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn ‘Uthman from ibn Sinan who has said the following. “I asked abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.), ‘Did Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, know Himself before He created the creation?’” The Imam (a.s.) replied, “Yes, He knew Himself.”

I further asked, “Did He see and hear His Own Self?” The Imam replied, “Allah did not need such things because He did not ask or demand it. He is His Own self and His Own self is He. His power is dominant and He does not need to name His Own self.

He chose His Own name for the sake of others so they can call Him. Until one is not called by means of his names he is not recognized. The fist name He chose for His Own self was al-‘Ali al-‘Azim (the Most High, the Great) because He is above all things. It then means that Allah and His name al-‘Ali al-‘Azim is His. The Most High, He is above all things.
